Hello Alon,

Please see some additional information on top of what Riin has shared. I hope this will help clarify the overall picture.

There is no legal requirement mandating the use of personal codes, emails, or other identifiers as usernames; we're given the choice to use our approach. For several years, we have been using this approach, which has proven to be highly efficient, as emails are not utilised as frequently here compared to the EU or other countries, and the local population often does not provide accurate email addresses. If we suddenly switch to using emails, drivers will likely resist, as they typically create emails just for signing up and then forget them. This would also create a huge additional workload for both Customer Support and Operations to do the workaround while negatively impacting our city metrics now and later. Switching from personal codes to emails at this time would be an undesirable move as we are in a heavy battle for market shares, and we are not meeting the expected results possessed by the Senior Leadership. Like us, the two major players, Uber and Careem, also use personal codes as usernames in Saudi Arabia.

 - Personal identification numbers are given on the governmental level and written in their documents.
- Drivers register their emails at first, but after the account is activated in the system, they’re informed via SMS that their username is their personal ID number. We do not disclose it in SMS, they know what their ID codes are.

Kind Regards,
Rostislav

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi [~accountid:712020:08b06da9-e575-4305-ae55-2fa207541b5b] [~accountid:6155b83199b4b8006a66bfd8],  

The amount we need to compensate the costumer for is the following:

# SEK 1,991 according to the court decision; and
# Interest on the amount pursuant to section 6 of the Interest Act (1975:635) from 11 June 2024 *until payment is made*. 

For visibility, interest according to (2) above is +calculated in the following way+:

_(The amount from the court decision) x interest according to Sveriges Riksbank and the interest act (12 %) / 365 days_

The above would therefore mean: 

SEK 1,991 x 0,12 = SEK 238,98 / 365 days = 0,654739… ≈ SEK 0,65

*This means that the interest for each day that we have not made the payment amounts to approximately ≈ SEK 0,65*.

The above amount needs to be calculated in relation to how many days that has passed since June 11 (date of the court decision), which is dependent on when exactly you can make the payment.

*_Example_*: 30 days has passed since 11 June = 0,65 x 30 = SEK 19,5 in interest. This would mean that the payment would need to be SEK 1,991 + SEK 19,50 = SEK 2010,50.

However, given that the interest amount per day is a rounded amount, please rather make the payment with a few SEK extra rather than too few. Also, please provide a confirmation of payment once this has been resolved. 

Thanks!  

Best regards, Emelie

Let me know if you have any questions!

All the best

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *1 August 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Orders history*



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/nl-nl/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/nl-nl/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

We currently have the following dimensions of decision on how we approach time-varying coefficients:

* *Setting ls and eta.* These are the priors on how you define propensity of the GP to change. There’s following continuum for how you approach it:
** Set ls and eta to the *most rigid* propensity to move (*left* extreme)
*** Equal to having a static  model (i.e. our status quo)
** Set ls and eta to the *most flexible* propensity to move (*right* extreme):
*** Overfit the model and get most of the variance explained
*** Model not generalizable to predict (but we do not need it). 
*** Opportunity - get the extreme variants of what our ads impact could be (i.e. limits)
*** Drawback - most probably will not be able to solve the issue this way once we have large granularity (i.e. if we have spend on platform level it might be good, but how does the model behave once we have 8 channels or more)
*** Drawback - the model can actually start to interpret ads movement due to cost change as time-varying effect (which we have seen on short-run examples - Paris, March 2023). We do not want it (we assume that model should be choosing change in spend and not time to be 'prioritized' as explaining factor).
** Somewhere in the middle (question is how to define it - probably with simulations). 

*Interesting:* this idea is also explicitly mentioned in [this|https://arxiv.org/html/2408.07678v1] article. They also mention that you should choose a curved stationary model or a linear GP (which in our case is not considered as trouble)



* *Specifying effects as linear or curved*
** Curved:
*** gives opportunity to always be sure that we will end up with a curve as a result
*** Some examples show that curves can actually lead to more smooth GPs (Brussels, when spend reaches 0)
** Linear: 
*** there seems to be no guarantee that as a result of the study we will get results that will remind a curve
*** In our rebudgeting process we depend on the 'diminishing returns' assumption a lot (linear relation will cause us to spend infinity)



* *The amount of GPs and their similarity:*
** One GP for all ads impact (similar even for platforms - probably with some multiplier) <- Left extreme
** …
** Centered GPs for channels or platforms
** …
** Different and non-related GPs for all the channels

*Background:*

* In the first privacy advise received, it was recommended to opt for data storage in the EU: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/servicedesk/projects/LSS/queues/issue/LSS-8118|https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/servicedesk/projects/LSS/queues/issue/LSS-8118]
* Nevertheless, some of the data residency of our MixPanel (Bolt Food) is in the US. {color:#bf2600}*Issue:*{color} Is action required on our side to make sure data is moved to the EU? (Reflecting UBER decision) / How important is it that we move the data to the EU?



*Initial Review:*

For international personal data transfers we are required to ensure that there are appropriate safeguards for  adequate personal data protection by our vendors located outside the EU (and third countries without the Commission’s adequacy decision). In other words, it is our responsibility to verify that these {color:#006644}*vendors adhere to the same personal data protection standards as if GDPR applied to them*{color}. 

As a data controller, {color:#006644}*Bolt must be transparent ensure that users are aware*{color} what personal data we collect, what we use them for but also {color:#006644}*who are our processors and where will the data be stored or transferred to*{color}. Personal data processed by MixPanel (According to Schedule 1 of the DPA: [https://mixpanel.com/legal/dpa/|https://mixpanel.com/legal/dpa/|smart-link] ):

* City, Region, Country, Time zone, Browser, Browser Version Device, Current URL Initial Referrer, Initial Referring Domain Operating System Mixpanel Library Referrer, Referring Domain Screen Height Screen Width Search Engine Search Keyword, UTM Parameters (i.e., any UTM tags associated with the link a customer clicked to arrive at the domain), Last Seen (the last time a property was set or updated) of Bolt’s Users (both web and apps).

MixPanel’s DPA has SCCs in Schedule 2 with all clauses, except of Clause 7 (good).

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Full memo: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KHQC6NY0hzxPiJV2ROWrAmv0KSlz3Nnx/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KHQC6NY0hzxPiJV2ROWrAmv0KSlz3Nnx/edit|smart-link] 

Summary: 
Overall the competition law risk is low

*Exclusivity:*

* Popeyes’ restaurants could be exclusively available on the Bolt Food platform, excluding Wolt and other platforms from partnering with Popeyes in the Baltics
* But it is advised that the exclusivity arrangement *should not exceed 5 years* unless it can be demonstrated that a longer duration is necessary to recoup Popeyes’ specific investments. The shorter the exclusivity period, the less likely it is to have restrictive effects on competition.

*Non-Compete Clause:*
The proposed clause is generally in line with competition law, but to ensure full compliance, it is advised to:

* *Narrow the definition of “Competitor”* to include only those directly competing with Popeyes in the quick-service/fast food chicken and/or seafood-related business domain
* *Limit the geographical scope* to territories where the Popeyes franchise is already present.

______________
Above findings apply to both operating models:

# *Model 1:* Bolt enters into a franchise agreement with RBI to own the franchise and manage Popeyes’ operations in the Baltics.
# *Model 2:* Bolt and a local partner establish a joint venture (the “JV”). The JV enters into the franchise agreement with RBI. The franchise will be owned by the JV, but the local operations of Popeyes will be managed by the local partner.

However, If *Bolt starts operating the Popeyes franchise*, it would *enter the downstream market* for restaurants and become a direct competitor to Bolt Food partners (KFC, McDonald's, Burger King, etc.).

* This could have competition law implications, such as (i) potential exchange of commercially sensitive information; and/or (ii) abuses of dominant position (self-preferencing, refusal to supply etc.).
* The vertical restraints agreed upon between Bolt and its Bolt Food partners might no longer benefit from the Vertical Block Exemption Regulation.

Based on these considerations, from a competition law perspective, *Model 2, where Bolt is not operating the franchise, presents a lower risk*

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error.

[~accountid:60e01bd03136170077df0bb9], thanks for your time earlier today. Below is a summary of the key points to consider:

# *Facial recognition database*

* _Explicit, freely given and informed consent_ - collection and storage of biometric data requires user consent. Consent means allowing individuals to have a real choice and control over how their data is used. If they don’t have a true choice, the consent is not valid. People must be able to refuse consent without facing negative consequences and should be able to withdraw it easily at any time.
* The consent mechanism _should be separate_ from the existing selfie verification process, as it represents a separate processing activity (driver’s licence verification vs facial recognition database).
* The processing of biometric data poses a high risk to user privacy, so _prior consultation and approval_ by the Data Protection Inspectorate is mandatory. Given the sensitive nature of the data processing activity, it is highly unlikely that we will receive regulatory approval.

# *Selfie verification process*

* Selfies are not considered biometric data if they are processed manually. Therefore, the existing selfie verification feature is not problematic as long as we collect consent for automated processing and provide a manual verification option.
* Established consent mechanism should cover selfie and document liveness check and image quality check.
* We need to collect user's consent for each automated processing activity - we should display this screen for both DL and ID verifications every time. 
* In some flows, we ignore the user's lack of consent for automated processing:

Hey [~accountid:62b2cf3c0c77011bdfdcdbcd] 
With regards to the amendment to the Road Transport Act, we analysed this with the PP agency and:

* The only change indentified with regards to dispatch operators is as follows: _The holder of a taxi service license or holder of the permission for dispatching can submit a proposal for the granting of a new taxi service/dispatching license no earlier than three months before the expiry of the original license. (the permission is  issued for 10 years)._
* There were four other changes that were significant to our business, to which we submitted opinions during the legislative process:
** Vehicle of a taxi service can be just a vehicle registered in Slovakia, which license plate is registered within the driver's permission (koncesia vodiča). - §27 art. 17
** In case of transfer of possession of the vehicle or change of ownership of the vehicle to a person who is not the operator of the taxi service, the taxi service vehicle is removed from the vehicle register as of the day when the transfer of possession of the vehicle or change of ownership of the vehicle occurred. The taxi service vehicle certificate (osvedčenie vozidla taxislužby) becomes invalid on the day the taxi service vehicle is removed from the taxi service vehicle registry.
** The holder of a taxi service license (koncesia) or holder of the permission for dispatching can submit a proposal for the granting of a new taxi service/dispatching license no earlier than three months before the expiry of the original license.
** Vehicle, which does not meet the requirements outlined in §27 Art. 17 will be withdrawn from the taxi vehicle registry no later than on 31 December 2024.

Coming back here with my comments. As this is our product we will want to continue with our own template General Terms (GTC). Nevertheless we’re open to make amendments to it with our Special Terms. In case you have already concluded and shared with them our Special Terms, please attach it here as well.

I’m sure you’re well aware of our [Bolt Business playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+General+T+C+for+Bolt+Business.+Business+account], but just in case attaching it here also since it can be a huge help for negotiations. 

Now, the points they have brought up:

* *Term ‘contract’* - this is brought out in our GTC as they also point it out. The terms of the Special Terms are defined in GTC, where it’s brought out that the GTCs in whole is the Agreement. So their latter conclusion is correct, but of course in time there could be potentially amendments to the Special Terms which would also be integral part of the Agreement then.
* *BOLT does not guarantee that access will be uninterrupted or error-free* - This is something we cannot guarantee, bugs etc can occur. Of course we are doing our best all the time that the service would be error-free, but it’s still technology and should be fairly understandable why we can’t guarantee something like this. 
* *any failure of its systems that results in the failure or inability to provide the Bolt Services or Bolt Business* - Same as with the previous point, while working relentlessly for ultimate Customer satisfaction Bolt does not guarantee 100% uptime of its services.
* *business damage or loss of (Customer) profit* - We’re not liable for this as the service is provided by third-party drivers. 
* *Any purely economic, special, indirect or consequential losses, costs, damages, charges or expenses (of the Customer)* - Same as the last point.
* *The acts, errors or omissions of any third party providing its services through the Bolt Platform (e.g. driver...)* - Bolt is not liable for the third parties providing its services on Bolt platform (drivers, couriers, sellers of goods), i.e. in so far +as Bolt acts as a platform operator+. Bolt takes reasonable steps to ensure that such providers act in accordance with the law and the applicable industry standards.
* *May unilaterally change the terms and conditions* - Bolt shall notify the customer in due course before making any changes to the T&C. Should the customer not accept the changes then they are free to stop using the services without any sanctions. Any changes to the T&C do not affect any special terms agreed between Bolt and the Customer separately. We can also add a specific timeframe to the Special Terms for this.
* *Fees etc.* - As the Bolt Services are utilized by Users in the interests of the Customer, and Users are added/removed by the Customer then it’s only natural that Customer is also obliged to indemnify any damage or other exceptional cost caused by the User during its use of Bolt Services. It’s acceptable to add the following to the clause: _… Bolt shall provide documented evidence of such cost upon Customer request._
* *GTC clause 8.5* - please have a loot at this from the Playbook yourself also. We want flexibility to assign a part or all Bolt Business agreements automatically to a third party, e.g (in the unlikely scenario) that Bolt is purchased wholly or partially by a third party. On the other hand we’d prefer if Customer does not have such automatic right to make sure we know who our Customer is at all times. It is possible to change it to mutual also, but *please note that before making this suggestion it needs to be approved by the Regional Head of Sales.*

I will remain attentive to your further questions/comments. 🙂

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days

Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

hi [~accountid:5c09426d957a4e56aa49222f] , the legal assessement has already been done for Sweden:

_The feature of_ *_driver queue optimisation has been flagged by product legal as high risk_* _in terms of reclassification. This is because when using driver queue optimisation, the historic driver performances are used to “prioritise” or “de-prioritise” a driver in the “dispatch queue”, which may have the effect that “poor performers” will have less access to work as a result of Bolt’s discretion.However, the driver queue optimisation feature is slightly less risky than “acceptance rate blocking”. As we are already_ *_using acceptance rate blocking in Sweden, adding this into the mix probably isn't going to change our risk profile dramatically_*_._

As in Croatia the reclass risk is lower than in Sweden since it is a fleet market, I think we can move forward with this. 

Please note that it needs to be approved by the Privacy team. I’ve created a sub ticket for them.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18] let’s discuss this approach on our 1:1 tomorrow. 



*Purpose:* SMS reminders for appointment scheduling page through external SMS services provider - Twillio

*Relationship:* C-P but in relation to Bolt data (employee IDs, contact details) C-C



:green_circle: 

* For clients domiciled in the EU, we’re entering into the agreement with the EU entity located in Ireland
* SCCs are included (Schedule 3 of the DPA)
* No sale of any personal data by Twilio (Section 1 of Schedule 1 of the DPA)
* Sub-processors are listed and entered into contract with and Twilio is liable for their acts and omissions (Section 7 of the DPA)
* Data retention: will be returned / deleted after the termination (unless required by law)



🔴 

* The distinction between when Twilio is a separate controller or processor is tricky

||*Separate Controller*||*Processor*||
|*“Customer Account Data”* personal data relating to Bolt’s relationship with Twilio, including _names or contact information of Bolt’s employees_ authorized to access Bolt’s account for the purpose of their identity verification|Personal Data to process {color:#bf2600}user content{color} on our behalf and in accordance with our instructions; that being personal data exchanged as a result of Bolt using Twilio’s services.|
|*“Customer Usage Data”* personal data processed by Twilio for transmitting or exchanging text message bodies / media ({color:#bf2600}User Content{color}) through communication networks. E.g. includes data used to identify the source and destination of a communication, such as: _data subjects’ phone numbers, device location generated in the context of providing the Services, and the date, time, duration and the type of communication and activity logs used to identify the source of Service requests_.| |

→ {color:#bf2600}*Unclear when does Twilio act as a separate controller in processing “Customer Usage Data” and when as processor under Bolt’s instruction, since both activities process “User Content”*{color}. The only distinguishing factor is that Twilio is a processor when processing User Content under our instruction. Possible disputes / issues will therefore be very circumstantial, i.e. Has in that particular case Twilio acted under our instruction, or has Twilio been transmitting or exchanging the User Data? Isn’t “transmission” / “exchange” itself acting under our instruction? Therefore, I’d suggest treating any processing of “customer usage data” as if Twilio acted as the processor.

On the other hand, the risk of for instance soliciting our end users for direct marketing, or contacting them anyhow is remote, since Twilio engages in B2B services. 

* Bolt must ensure that the instructions comply with Applicable Data Protection Laws. While Twilio will inform us if they think our instructions violate any applicable law, it is our responsibility and we will not 
* The majority of Twilio’s sub-processors are located in the USA ([https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/sub-processors|https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/sub-processors|smart-link] + Section 7.(1)(b) of the DPA) but SCCs and Transfer Impact Assessments have been done – transparent (⚪  beige flag?)
* Liabilities and indemnification are unclear – Only mentions that neither party cannot be held responsible for administrative fine received by the other party for non-compliance with GDPR obligations (83 GDPR) (Section 4.3. of the DPA). The T&Cs also do not mention much in regards to personal data incidents or claims arising out of breaches of obligations. On the other hand, they seem to have robust procedures for helping satisfying DSRs at no extra cost (Section 8 of the DPA).
* {color:#bf2600}*The DPA and T&Cs are silent on indemnification of Bolt in respect to failure of Twilio to comply with its obligations*{color}
* Notification of data breaches no later than 72 hours. Quite tight. 



*Proposed Answer:*

From the Privacy standpoint, you may proceed with the agreement. There are a few details to keep in mind:

Bolt is not indemnified in respect to Twilio failing to comply with its obligations. This is particularly risky, since as Controller, we are accountable for the actions of our Processors. Moreover, Section 5.1. of the DPA is silent on the requirement of documented instructions to Twilio: It is therefore extremely important that we always give Twilio documented instructions in writing. This is a requirement under GDPR and will keep us covered as much as possible in the event of Twilio breaching its obligations or not acting based on our instructions.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin.

Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

The preauthorisation is automatically released when the payment is successfully captured or cancelled. 

Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

We will close this case in 5 days. 
If you still require assistance then please leave a comment on the ticket.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Jfrog xray analysis service  has a process for keeping up to date csvv score: [https://jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-security-documentation/cvss-scoring-in-xray|https://jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-security-documentation/cvss-scoring-in-xray|smart-link] so in short it’s processing big batches in case of any big update that leads to high memory utilization. 

The status of it may be checked with: 

{noformat}curl   -H "Authorization: Bearer token" https://registry.live.boltint.net/xray/api/v1/migration/cvssV3/status
{"status":"enable_running","status_msg":"CVSS V3 enable migration is running"}%{noformat}

This process happened randomly, and don’t have any metrics around it, so bumped instances type to keep it running for now. Maybe in future xray may be migrated to k8s, what will make scaling of it more easier, but will see.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Updated envoy configuration, checked with internal IT, and all is working.

Hey [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] , 

I've been talking to local operators in Romania, and I'd like your opinion on whether it's possible to copy their model for the Access category or not.


In fact, we could potentially set up the kick back on the category if we set it up.
On the other hand, in Romania the category does not cover electric wheelchairs, only folding models. They have drawn up a list of all the vehicles compatible with this category. This takes into account the vast majority of our vehicles in France, as all cars with a large enough boot have access to the category. 

This is the message from a Romanian local operator : 

“In Romania, a standard wheelchair, which can be folded, fits in most cars (unless the car is very small). However, electric wheelchairs require special vehicles, which Bolt does not have. As long as there are physical limitations, Bolt cannot accommodate them.
 There is no law requiring the transport of disabled people using electric wheelchairs that do not fit in an ordinary car. These people require special conditions that Bolt is unable to provide.”

So, can we legally set up an ‘Access’ category in France that does not take into account all types of disability?

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Proposed article:

*Note:* See 🚗 [+Pre-authorization logic+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005100694], 🥡 🥕 [+Pre-authorization logic+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019860520] and 🛴 [+Pre-authorization logic+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7108948722962] for more information about pre-authorization.

----

*Release process*

* The pre-auth is usually canceled when the system runs the actual charge. In this case, the payment status changes from auth to capture.
* In the unusual event that the eater reports that their pre-auth was not released/returned/canceled, inform them that it can take between 1 to 30 business days, depending on their bank’s release process.
* If after the maximum bank release process time has passed, the eater still has this pending hold on their account, ask them to contact their bank to initiate the release process.

----

h3. *Step 1:* Check the Payment Status

* Payment Status is: *Captured*, *Canceled*, *Failed* or *Chargeback*
** The authorized amount has been released from our side and most likely the authorized amount has been returned to the customer
** If the authorized amount has not been returned to the user, it could take up to 30 days for some banks to return the funds
** If the authorized amount is still not returned after 30 days, continue to *Step 3*
* Payment Status is: *Authorized and it has been more than 72 hours* for Micromobility
** Continue to *Step 3*
* Payment Status is: *Authorized and it has been more than 24 hours* for Delivery and Rides
** Continue to *Step 3*

h3. *Step 2*: Share the pre-authorisation number and ask the customer to check with their bank

How to find the pre-authorization reference number:

* For Adyen, it is available as an acquirer reference on the _payment attempts_ page.
** _Payment_ > _Attempts_ > _Authorisation_ > _authorize_ > _search for acquirer reference_

Example of the pre-authorization reference number:

!https://camo.githubusercontent.|width=506,height=36,alt="example"!

* If you found the reference number - share it with the user and advise them to contact their bank
* If there is no reference number - advise the user to contact their bank
** The pre-authorization release duration depends on the rider's bank release process
** The same applies for 3rd party payments (Apple Pay, PayPal, etc.)
* If the user comes back with information from their bank continue to the *Step 3*

h3. *Step 3*: Escalate the issue to Commerce team via SD

User may return with information from their bank indicating that they should contact us. If 14 days have passed since the end of the ride and the bank has directed the user to us:

Escalate to the Commerce team via [+SD+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/-1] if all of the below requirements have been met: 

* The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank
* The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 
* Other cases to escalate to the Commerce team
** User provided proof pre-authorization has not been released
** The user has a large number of unreleased pre-authorizations
** You collected data on unreleased pre-authorizations affecting a large number of customers from a specific bank or a country

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

# Our external counsels in Romania will provide support regarding booking appointment with the local notary. The price for this would be 360 EUR. The appointment with the notary can be secured within the same week as the request is made.

“Dear Floyd,

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *13 August 2024*.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person.

[~accountid:5b7bea6c358c9f2a008eab3e] hey, getting back to you.

* We can report unjustified cancellation reasons to the council without issues.
* The problem occurs when the cancellation reasons involve information that, when combined with other data, could constitute sensitive personal data (e.g., details about a passenger's disability or religious clothing). While these details alone may not identify someone, adding specific drop-off/pick-up locations, dates, times, or direct identifiers (like names or emails) introduces significant privacy risks, as sensitive personal data requires enhanced protection and often consent.
* The key advice is to share as little data as possible. If the council only needs the driver's data and the reasons for cancellation, that’s all we should provide. We strongly advise against sharing any additional passenger information.
* If additional information is absolutely necessary (e.g., the date of the cancellation), we must ensure we have a strong, objective reason for doing so, such as the council needing it to verify the date of blocking or to give the driver an option to appeal.



Bottom line - We can proceed as long as we are aligned on the points above.

Hey [~accountid:712020:770b0a51-ce61-48b4-990c-622be4e099ce], 

I don’t know if you noticed the last response given in the CCM-16926 ticket, so I will put it here as well. 

{quote}After safety related issue is resolved should the Agent change severity level to Tier 1 and None, and then deal with non-safety issue or not, as this becomes a non-safety issue.{quote}

If a case contains both a safety and a non-safety issue, the case doesn’t become a non-safety case once the safety part is solved. If it’s a safety case, the severity shouldn’t be removed unless a process states otherwise. The same goes for issue tags. The tier can change depending on whether the agent who initially handled the case is trained to deal with non-safety issues or not: 

* If yes - the case remains in the safety tier with the applicable severity even if there is a non-safety issue, but the agent should add the relevant non-safety issue tags. 
* If the agent is not trained to solve the non-safety part - the case needs to be escalated to Tier 1, but the severity will not change, and safety issue tags will remain on the case. Tier 1 agent will add the relevant non-safety tags.

As mentioned before, we’re revamping all of the safety workflows, including the safety escalation guidelines. We’re currently in the final stages of this, so we will not be updating the existing guidelines. However, once released, the reviewed articles should give fuller clarity on how to handle such cases, as they will be based on a step-by-step concept.

I hope this answers your question, but let me know if anything else is unclear. 🙂

Hey [~accountid:5bdbfc9b359ddf204e8c7e02] 
The Alcohol Act provides that 
- "_a person_ *_transferring_* _an alcoholic beverage_ *_or handing_* _an alcoholic beverage_ *_over_* _may demand identification from the recipient and_ *_refuse to hand the alcoholic_* _beverage over_ *_in case of failure to present such identification_*_"._ Whereas voluntary guidelines issued by Kaupmeeste liidu require a check of the ID of customers who look younger than 30. Thus, a in usual set up a courier shall always check the ID of the client who looks younger than 30 years.
- Applying this requirement to robot delivery, I believe the proposed solution (requesting the customer to take a selfie and a photo of a valid ID) is appropriate, *provided we always request this ID and selfie check at the handover of the alcohol*, regardless of whether the customer has previously uploaded their ID and completed a selfie-check on the Bolt app. This check is required not only by law but also because, in practice, the person receiving the alcohol from the robot might not be the one who placed the order (it could be a minor). Since the robot cannot objectively assess the person, the selfie and ID check is the only viable option.

In conclusion, I see the solution as follows: we request customers to provide the selfie and ID (i) before ordering alcohol via the Bolt app (regardless of whether they choose a standard courier or robot delivery) and (ii) upon picking up the alcohol order from the robot.

Please share your thoughts on the above. Thank you!

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days.

It's quite a tricky situation.

Initially, while we were discussing this with Asia, we agreed that the agents should follow the correct process and if the process says that we shouldn't offer any comps, then that's it.

But I also discussed this with Michaela from the Quality team, and she thinks from the customer perspective it would be frustrating if at the beginning there was compensation offered, but then it was refused 🤔 maybe the user rejected the refund because they were unhappy with the amount of it, then when the ticket goes to CS it means that they are getting nothing at all (even not what was offered at the beginning?). 

I also tried to investigate why Alfred would even offer an incorrect refund, and according to [+this thread+ |https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05DDLBUR0A/p1725635339945729?thread_ts=1725357132.365269&cid=C05DDLBUR0A]it was designed to do that on purpose. 

This emphasizes that we should decide on what to do in these cases because this is not even considered an issue.

Decided to check with Legal if we are allowed to refuse what was already offered - yes, we are legally allowed to refuse the compensation that was offered to the customer before.

There is also [this old conversation|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04LU7CDY49/p1684829099290609] between Matilda and the Heads - seems like the approach was to refuse the compensation, but have a place where the incorrect automation should be reported - most probably will go with this option.

Will see if I can get more [context|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05DDLBUR0A/p1725977931820649?thread_ts=1725357132.365269&cid=C05DDLBUR0A] on why the automation was made that way and if there is a chance to change that, but will also note to include this scenario in the non-safety case handling process if all the automation are supposed to work the way they do.

[~accountid:5bdbfc9b359ddf204e8c7e02]I understand, but I see a risk that robot delivery could be exploited. For example, an adult could place an alcohol delivery request via robot to a different address (one where there are no adults). In practice, this could result in alcohol being delivered to an address where only minors are present. A robot cannot assess or detect this situation if no selfie and ID check is required upon handover. Is it technically possible to order a delivery to an address other than the one where the person placing the order is located? If so, the risk of exploiting robot deliveries becomes very real in my opinion.

Another risk is that under Estonian law, selling or handing over alcohol to intoxicated individuals is prohibited. The responsibility lies with the seller, and in the case of deliveries, with the couriers. However, how do we detect intoxication in the case of robot deliveries? This increases the risk that intoxicated individuals may start using robot delivery, knowing that a robot, unlike a courier, cannot assess or refuse delivery due to signs of intoxication. [~accountid:5bdbfc9b359ddf204e8c7e02], do we have a technological solution for this? I doubt the technology is sophisticated enough to detect if the person picking up alcohol appears intoxicated.

In general, non-compliant solutions could be introduced and stay in place if the business is aware of the risks and still wants to proceed, until the authorities or media spot non-compliance or problematic cases (like the ones mentioned above). But we need to be aware that it could potentially provoke media discussions, framing Bolt as contributing to alcohol-related problems in society, which could put us in a negative light.

https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin.

A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

Analysis in the clarification stage

Product Requirement

* It’s a by design strong requirement to have two type of approvals roles: Manager and Permission Owner.
* There is a {color:#bf2600}missing specification{color} for the use case when an person belongs to the both categories: Manager and Permission Owner
* Currently, in this situation, the manager has to approve two requests, one as Manager, and another one as Permission Owner
* While we target to improve the UX and reduce the number of clicks, there are some grounded requirements
** There must be always two type of requests, so such an option to *send only the Manager request or only the Permission Owner request is out of question*
* So that, we could explore two options
** One request approval approves the other one automatically 
** The Permission Owner request do not include the manager, so the manager will evaluate only the Manager request 


*Option 1* - requests auto-sync evaluation 

* From the implementation perspective, it’s supposed to listen for one event, and automatically propagate the status to the other one 
* Considering we rely on a dependency service (RnA)
** We’ve to alter the RnA service to accept requests evaluation by internal endpoints, so system and not human input
** The audit traces are impacted, we don’t see clearly who’s the user 
** The requests could get out of sync if the update to the second request fails systematically 
** One option would be to implement the *grouping of requests abstraction* to RnA service, so RnA could apply the change atomically to the both requests
* It’s a big effort - it could go up to 2-3 weeks



*Option 2* - the Permission Owner request do not include the manager

* While the implementation effort goes down to 3 days, it still looks like a hack that could question why the permission owner list does NOT include all the owners



Business Value 

* Randomly checking the requests it doesn’t look like a common use case to have a manager in both roles. Building a thorough and conclusive report requires a big effort. 
* So, with the limited data on the table, the implementation doesn’t bring up consistent value company wise compared with the effort, at least for Option 1.



Conclusion  

* From the above options, Option 2 might be feasible from the Job Size perspective, but it’s more a product owner decision because essentially we want to change an use case 
** When the system sends a permission request
** And a person is both a manager and permission owner
** Expect the manager to receive both requests and to approve/reject each of them individually
** *New Expect: <to fill in by the product owner>*

Then CS should proceed with contacting the driver (using the original driver details) and follow the same process to restore their accounts.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:478f91ed-c5e9-4914-a896-f1dcd7f9bb1d]! Thank you for your patience and kind reminder.

I have reviewed information about Bolt Rewards. As you know, the main risk we see in relation to such features is reclassification risk - i.e. probability that Bolt will be regarded as an employer of drivers. In Romania drivers are engaged through fleets and we have a bit more room for manoeuvre, but this is not 100% protection for us and we should assess risks without heavily relying on the fact that drivers work for fleets. There are a few problematic areas in connection to Bolt Rewards:

# Enrolment - As mentioned by Sorina, enrolment to Bolt Rewards should be voluntary. Ideally, we should communicate this opportunity to fleets and let them decide whether to join Bolt Rewards.
# Metrics - I understand that we wish to link rewards to drivers' acceptance rate and their score. This increases our risk of reclassification. It is therefore recommended to use as a metric the number of finished rides. This way we are not blocking their access to work.
# Value of benefits - If the benefits offered as part of this feature will significantly impact expenses of drivers we will increase the risk of reclassification, because we will significantly affect their earning capacity. Therefore, it is recommended to have lower value benefits that are nice, but do not in a significant way affect drivers' earnings.
# Internal benefits - we need to make sure that benefits we provide do not look like benefits provided from employer to their employee. Due to our relationship being with the fleet we should provide fleet the benefits such as faster CS support. If benefits are provided directly to drivers this increases our reclassification risk. 

Considering all of the above comments - if you proceed with launching Bolt Rewards and opt-in all drivers automatically, link rewards with acceptance rates and their score, offer benefits that can significantly reduce their operating costs and provide special treatment to drivers entitled to high rank benefits - there is a high probability that in case there will be a claim made by a driver to consider Bolt as its employer we will have a hard time defending it. 

You can proceed with launching Bolt Rewards, but it is recommended to take safer approach, because Romania is a medium risk level country and we need to be cautious.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

** Click  _Process Refund_

* Compensate the user
** On the Order page, click _Process Refund_

** Select _Bolt_ as the Actor at Fault
