Hi [~accountid:712020:d2041a9e-5593-41bd-9df9-49b17a6c735f],

Unfortunately, it is not possible to reissue the invoice if the rider’s profile was updated to add a work profile after a trip was taken. This is regulated by Polish law, i.e. it is not lawful to issue a VAT invoice for a service if the NIP number was not provided at the time of provision of service.

As the waiting time for tip and payment method capture is rather a global setting, I doubt there is any wiggle room for especially on market level. [~accountid:712020:2432bf62-c6bc-4b10-85a8-ef21c78a1e56] perhaps you could also check with engineering team if there is a possibility to reduce the ‘tip awaiting’ time from 15 to 10 for example. Just to show good-will to the authorities.

Hi team, 

The customer is reporting an incremental authorization. 

Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

Dear Salman 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *02 July 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* Communication history

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Hey, [~accountid:627cd418f29dcb0068f96508]! Thanks for these details. I have also checked your comments in the campaign T&Cs. Your answers raise some Privacy and IP concerns regarding the set up. Please let me consult with our Privacy and IP teams to make sure we do this thing right. I have already contacted them and I hope to hear from them soon. Meanwhile, we can finalise the mechanics of the campaign. I will comment in T&Cs document separately, but here is what concerns agreement with the agency:

# Instagram content - 4 stories and 1 reel, topics and instructions to be provided by Bolt. No concerns here. 
# Special delivery - food is provided by Bolt.
## Choice of food - analysis of food orders history is a privacy concern, I flagged this to them and let’s see what they say. Alternatives: Bolt selects something or allows winner to select. I recommend allowing winner to select within a specific budget due to these benefits: 1) this will create clarity as to the campaign value for tax purposes; 2) Bolt will not be liable for choosing a “wrong” dish that can make eater allergic etc.
## Delivery - times and location will be agreed by communicating with the winner. There is a privacy concern regarding collecting information about the address, I raised it with the privacy. 
## Location - Bolt will need to compensate travel expenses of the singer to the extent agreed with the agency. We may potentially limit participants to specific cities in the T&Cs, but at the moment it can be any place in Romania.
## Recording delivery - taking photos of the singer and winner raises privacy concerns, we will get this clarified.
# Dinner - food is provided by Bolt.
## Choice of food - same concerns as for special delivery. Here you also need to take into account dietary needs of the singer, so menu has to be pre-agreed. This has also privacy concerns as dietary requirements is personal information and we need it regarding both the winner and singer if we are choosing the food.
## Premises - hosting a dinner at winner’s place may have complications -what if the place is not nice, winner will have extra burden of making it clean and tidy, it can be too far away, singer may not be comfortable with attending a private place, what if the winner has no legal rights to be at that place - we cannot check that. The recommended course of action is to organise it at some public place where Bolt will be in control of risks. 
## Organisation - someone has to organise everything - delivery of food, presentation etc. Will we order catering or local team will do that?
## Location - Bolt will need to compensate travel expenses of the singer to the extent agreed with the agency. 
## Duration - to avoid any surprises it is better to plan the event time wise and pre-agree with the agency how much time is allocated for the event.
# Photos and videos - I will consult with our IP team on how to better word this in the contract and discuss this with the Privacy team as well.
# Use of photo/logo on delivery bags etc. - Same as above.

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hello [~accountid:712020:f43809ec-d863-4a84-bd49-caea9501cb9f] 

This is a worldwide accounting concept called “rounding”. It is a glitch that is not unique to Bolt. To explain it briefly, we show the balance entries with 2 decimals in admin (i.e. 31.78), however in the system it has more decimals (i.e. 31,784). In Driver Portal, it is shown with 1 decimal only (i.e. 31.8). So when decimals get less, the system rounds it up/down to the closest number.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *16 August 2024*.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

In your request, you specifically asked for the full order history for the period since the creation of your account. Therefore, we are providing the following information regarding the personal data we hold about you, to which you are entitled:

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *16 August 2024*.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

In your request, you specifically asked for the full order history for the period since the creation of your account. Therefore, we are providing the following information regarding the personal data we hold about you, to which you are entitled:

* *A file containing the full order history since creation of your account.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*The Data Subject’s rights*

The Data Subject has the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning him or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email. 

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt”

Sincerely,
Bolt”

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method.

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

When looking into refunds that only had 1 dish (menu item with no parent), and that dish was refunded, there are 2 types of users that get this kind of refunds:

* Users with 2 or more refunds: In all cases verified, it is evident fraud with recurring patterns and unlikely reported events.
* Users that have their first refund of this kind: this can refer to missing parts of a combo, or an insufficient quantity of an item (e.g. count of chicken strips). This is not unlikely. Roughly 1/4 of these users have unlikely reported events (main component is fully missing), and they make up 90% of the 28.6k eur spent on refunds over 3 months on these cases.

Thus, about 9.3k is spent monthly on suspicious refunds for 1 dish orders. Further analysis needs to be made on a bigger sample to more accurately assess the share of suspicious reports from 1 case users. Depending on the findings, we might recommend sending these cases to manual support when the issue key is missing item and the basket only contains 1 dish.

With 24R2, the Time Zones feature is now opt-in in both Preview and Production environments. 
 
 REPORTING 
With this release, reports are evaluated in the context of the time zone of the user running the report. Previously, all reports were evaluated only in Pacific Time Zone. When the user selects an Effective as of Date while running a report, that date is interpreted as midnight on that date in the user’s local time zone. This improves reporting accuracy for users located in time zones ahead of Pacific Time. 
Note: If you’ve previously opted into the Time Zones feature, you’ll automatically get the new reporting and EIB functionalities in your tenant.

Use Pacific Time Zone for Moments Check Box 
With 24R2, we add a new Use Pacific Time Zone for Moment check box in the Prompts tab on the Edit Custom Report task. This check box enables a user to determine if the effective moment is interpreted in Pacific Time Zone. If the check box is clear, the effective moment processes in the user’s local time zone. This check box is available when you select the Prompt for effective as of date option from the Effective Date field. 
 Effective Moment Report Field 
We deliver a new Effective Moment report field on the Global business object (secured to the Public Reporting Items domain), that you can use in your custom reports to enter an Effective as of Date date and return a moment that lines up with midnight: 
 

* In the user’s time zone for users behind Pacific Time 
* Pacific Time for users at or ahead of Pacific Time 


 This report field enables users west of Pacific Time to properly report on local dated data, while preserving moment based reporting for users east of Pacific Time. This report field is an alternative approach to using the Use Pacific Time Zone for Moments check box in your reports. 
 Note: An effective moment is defined when a transaction or process becomes effective as of a date, a time, and a time zone component. For example: Role Assignments are an example of an effective moment. Manager A is assigned their new role effective January 1, 2024 at midnight Pacific Time. At this same moment in Hawaii, the Manager A role becomes effective on December 31, 2023 at 9:00 PM in Hawaii Standard Time. 
 EIB INTEGRATIONS 
Effective dates and related data that you extract from a custom report by running an outbound EIB with an effective date prompt, now align with the same data that you extract using a direct report URL. 
 
 ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS 
As you explore the Time Zones feature, consider: 

* Workday determines a worker's location based on their primary position. 
* The worker's time zone is determined in the order of: • The worker's preferred time zone 
* The worker's primary position location 
* The tenant default time zone 
* PST 


 

* Workday doesn't set the time zone you specify for a worker if: • They aren't in the role-based security group for that time zone. 
* They don't have a primary position location, in which case their time zone is set to the tenant default. 
* There isn’t a tenant default. Workday uses PST as their time zone. 


 

* The feature doesn't support integrations. ISUs will continue to evaluate as of PST. 
* If needed, you can reverse the setup of the Time Zones feature in the Maintain Feature Opt-In report. If you opt out, workers who have just been assigned their role in a time zone ahead of PST have to wait until PST catches up to the date in their time zone, in order to regain access to their events in progress.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. I ran a rough estimate on how much we’re overpaying per week. 

here are the conditions I considered in my estimation:

* probably my *biggest* assumption is that all orders that have a price below £5 per hour are being underpaid. meaning that the price doesn’t match the order duration. 
** example orders:
*** [https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/529361687|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/529361687]
*** [https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/529808832|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/529808832]
*** [https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/531355616|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/531355616]
* I didn’t calculate the national minimum wage based on the driver’s real age like we’re supposed to based on the [UK government site|https://www.gov.uk/national-minimum-wage-rates]. I’ve considered all drivers to be 21+ years old, which means their minimum hourly age in the query is £11.44. 
* the top_up calculation takes the driver’s net earnings: *weekly earnings + incentives - Bolt service fee - vehicle expenses - tolls*
** for the sake of simplification, I only deducted a 25% commission and the tips. so in my query, the driver’s net earnings are 75% of the order prices minus tips. my assumption is that vehicle expenses and tolls have higher values than incentives. if that assumption is correct, my results will be smaller than the real values. I would be underestimating how much we’re overpaying. 

out of all drivers that got a {{national_living_wage_topup}}, I pull every order that satisfies the above conditions. then, if the sum of these orders is equal to or higher than the amount compensated, I consider the whole amount compensated as overpaid. if the sum is smaller than the amount compensated, then I take only the top_up sum from these orders alone. 

and these are the results:

!Screenshot 2024-09-12 at 16.12.06.png|width=520,height=147,alt="Screenshot 2024-09-12 at 16.12.06.png"!

I estimate we’re overpaying around *1.9k GBP per week*, or around *10k euros per month*.

ROUND(CASE WHEN y.sum_top_up_amount_gbp >= y.compensation_amount_gbp THEN y.compensation_amount_gbp ELSE y.sum_top_up_amount_gbp END,2) AS overpaid_amount_gbp
FROM (
SELECT 
x.driver_id,
x.comp_date,
x.compensation_amount_gbp,
SUM(x.top_up_amount_gbp) AS sum_top_up_amount_gbp
FROM (
WITH driver_compensations AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
a.created_date,
a.to_agent_id AS driver_id,
a.sum AS compensation_amount_gbp
FROM ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record a
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2024-08-01'
AND a.to_agent_type = 'driver'
AND a."type" = 'national_living_wage_topup'
--AND a.to_agent_id = 2607478
)
SELECT 
co.order_id,
co.driver_courier_id AS driver_id,
co.created_date AS order_date,
dc.created_date AS comp_date,
(DATE_DIFF('minute',ot.driver_accepted,ot.finished)*11.44/60) AS min_wage_amount,											-- 1st rough adjustment: all drivers are 21+ old https://www.gov.uk/national-minimum-wage-rates
(co.partner_price - COALESCE(co.tips_amount,0))*0.75 AS rough_net_earnings,													-- 2nd rough adjustment: net earnings amount isn't subtracting tolls or vehicle expenses and it's also not summing incentives. 
ROUND(((DATE_DIFF('minute',ot.driver_accepted,ot.finished)*11.44/60) - (co.partner_price*0.75 - COALESCE(co.tips_amount,0))),2) AS top_up_amount_gbp,
CASE WHEN MIN(DATE_DIFF('day',co.created_date,dc.created_date)) >= 0 AND MIN(DATE_DIFF('day',co.created_date,dc.created_date)) < 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS driver_got_paid,
CASE WHEN DATE_DIFF('day',co.created_date,dc.created_date) >= 0 AND DATE_DIFF('day',co.created_date,dc.created_date) < 7 THEN dc.compensation_amount_gbp ELSE 0 END AS compensation_amount_gbp
FROM ng_public.fraud_order_check foc
JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co ON foc.order_id = co.order_id AND foc.city_id = co.city_id 
JOIN ng_public.etl_fact_company_order_try_state_log_transposed ot ON ot.order_id = co.order_id AND ot.city_id = co.city_id 
JOIN driver_compensations dc ON dc.driver_id = co.driver_courier_id 
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2024-08-01'
AND CAST(foc.created_date_hour AS date) >= date '2024-08-01'
AND ot.created_date >= date '2024-08-01'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.country_code = 'gb'
AND co.partner_price*1.00/(DATE_DIFF('minute',ot.driver_accepted,ot.finished)*1.00/60) <= 5									-- 3rd rough adjustment: orders below 5 gbp per hour are underpriced
AND co.driver_courier_id = 2607478 
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9
) AS x
WHERE x.driver_got_paid = 1 
GROUP BY 1,2,3
) AS y 
GROUP BY 1,2,3
) AS z 
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us.

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Invoice history*

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,
